title: Weekly Market Update: Hawkish Fed, Big Tech Earnings and Middle East Risks · Inter&Co Blog
summary: Markets navigated a hawkish Fed pause, strong cloud results from Microsoft and Amazon, weakness in AI-related stocks, rising oil prices, and anticipation for July's Nonfarm Payrolls report.
body_text: Last week (July 27–31, 2026) was defined by three main drivers: a hawkish Fed pause, big tech earnings amid selling in AI stocks, and the Middle East war escalation. The Fed held rates at 3.50%–3.75% but surprised with a 9-3 split vote favoring a hike, sending the 30-year Treasury yield to its highest since 2007, around 5.25%. Mid-week, semiconductors cratered toward their worst month since 2002, dragging the Nasdaq into correction territory. By Friday, Microsoft (+16%) and Amazon (+15%) triggered a powerful recovery — both their cloud businesses reported very strong results — lifting the S&P 500 +1.0% and Nasdaq +1.6% on the week. Apple (-8.5%) and Meta (-7%) disappointed on guidance and cash flow. Oil surged above $90 as Iran rejected a ceasefire proposal. Gold held near $4,060, Bitcoin around $64,000, and the DXY dollar fell 1.5%. For the week ahead, July Nonfarm Payrolls is the key data point — markets price a 60-70% chance of a September Fed hike. On the geopolitical front, during the weekend Trump called off what he said would be a major strike in Iran, bringing back hopes of a peace deal soon.

title: Five Pre-Construction Bottlenecks AI Clears Before Breaking Ground
summary: Running construction projects is complicated. We make it simple.
body_text: Insight Most construction projects are won or lost long before anyone breaks ground. The first decisions get made in pre-construction. Which bids to pursue, which risks to price, which subcontractors to involve, which terms to accept. Those choices shape the whole project, and they get made under time pressure with thousands of pages of documents on the table. Construction still has a productivity problem that makes this harder than it should be. Brickanta's report The Cost of Standing Still estimates that weak productivity leaves roughly SEK 164 billion in foregone value every year in Swedish construction, and finds that professionals spend 35 percent of their time on non-value-adding work, including 5.5 hours a week just searching for project information. Most of that waste lives at the desk, where the bid package grows and teams have to decide quickly. That is where a construction AI earns its place. Here are five ways it changes the work. 1. Bid review that reads everything, every time A bid package can run to hundreds or thousands of pages of drawings, provisions, specifications, schedules, and appendices. The risks are rarely obvious. They hide in a phrase that quietly shifts a responsibility or a drawing that puts the ceiling at three metres against a description that says 2.7. Manual review forces a tradeoff every time about what gets read closely, what gets skimmed, and what someone trusts has already been checked. A construction-specific agent reads the full package, compares documents against each other, and flags what deserves human attention. The team still decides whether to bid. They just decide it having seen the whole package rather than the parts they had time for. 2. Estimate review that catches what the spreadsheet misses A missed requirement, an underestimated quantity, or a mispriced risk goes beyond the spreadsheet. It follows the project all the way to final inspection and lands on the margin. A construction-specific agent extracts quantities and requirements from the drawings and specifications, checks them against the estimate, and flags the gaps. A requirement that was never priced, a schedule that doesn't match the scope, a ground condition buried in a geotechnical report. The estimator still owns the number. Anticipating even one change order before the bid goes in can be enough to pay for the work. 3. Subcontractor packages in minutes instead of days Once a bid is won, the main contractor has to procure a subcontractor for every trade, and each trade needs its own focused package. The painter has no use for the electrical drawings. The window supplier doesn't need every floor plan. On a large project there can be hundreds of these procurement categories, and assembling them by hand is slow, repetitive work. An agent that knows which drawings and documents each trade actually needs can build every trade-specific package from the full document set in minutes. That gives the procurement team the time back to negotiate, compare suppliers, and protect the schedule. 4. Contract review before the risk locks in The most important legal work usually happens before the contract is signed. The team needs to know which standard contract applies, where the project departs from AB 04 or ABT 06, and which clauses push risk onto the contractor. A warranty stretched from five to ten years, or a penalty clause with no cap, reads very differently before signing than after. A construction-specific agent makes contract review a normal part of bid review, flagging deviations, unclear responsibility, and clauses that carry legal weight, with every flag traceable to the exact page, paragraph, and phrase it came from. The lawyer still makes the judgment. The agent gets the lawyer in earlier, with a clearer view of what matters. 5. Knowledge that stays when people leave Most of what a construction company knows lives in finished projects, old estimates, past change-order lists, and the memory of experienced people. When a collegue leaves, much of it walks out the door. Turning past projects into searchable reference material keeps that knowledge in the company. Every new bid can be checked against what the firm has already lived through, so the team gets a relevant answer quickly instead of digging through archives or hoping someone remembers. The common thread: better decisions, earlier None of this replaces people. The estimator still prices the job, the lawyer still owns the legal call, the project manager still owns the client. What a construction AI changes is when the decisions get made and how much the team knows when they make them. The tool does have to be built for construction. Pasting sensitive bid documents into a general chatbot creates new risk, with no data control and no way to trace an answer back to its source. A construction platform needs governance, source references, and data control, so every flag and summary links back to the document it came from. The tools are here. The open question is how long contractors can afford to review bids, build estimates, and prepare procurement without them. Request a demo to see what Brickanta can do with your next bid package.

title: What is Fleet Management Software? How It Works and Key Benefits
summary: Fleet management software tracks vehicles and equipment, cuts fuel waste, and prevents downtime. See how it works, its key benefits, and what to look for.
body_text: TL;DR: One-Minute Brief Fleet management software is a platform that gives fleet managers full visibility into their operations by tracking vehicles and equipment, monitoring fuel and maintenance activity, scoring driver safety, and generating reports from one connected system. The features that matter most are real-time analytics, AI-driven insight, fuel loss detection, predictive maintenance, driver behavior scoring, route optimization, and contract management, because together they turn scattered fleet data into decisions that reduce cost, downtime, and risk. Key takeaways What is fleet management software? It’s a platform that tracks vehicles and equipment, monitors fuel and maintenance, and scores driver safety, all from one connected system. Real-time tracking gives fleet managers live visibility across every vehicle and machine, instead of a monthly rollup that is already out of date. Fuel monitoring and predictive maintenance catch problems, such as a fuel loss or a developing failure, early enough to act before they turn costly. A smart fleet relies on AI-driven insight, driver behaviour scoring, and compliance tracking working together, not as separate tools. Platforms like TENDERD bring tracking, fuel, maintenance, and safety data into a single system, so decisions do not depend on switching between disconnected tools. Introduction Running a fleet today means more than knowing where a vehicle is. Fleet managers are expected to control fuel costs, keep drivers safe, catch maintenance issues before they turn into breakdowns, and prove all of it to finance and compliance teams, often from a spreadsheet that is already a week out of date. Fleet management software exists to close that gap, giving teams one place to see what is happening across their vehicles and equipment instead of piecing it together after the fact. The category has moved fast. Where early platforms mainly plotted a dot on a map, modern fleet management software pulls in live telemetry, driver behaviour data, fuel sensors, and maintenance records, then uses ai to flag what actually needs attention. The result is a shift from reacting to problems to catching them early enough to do something about them. This guide walks through the features that matter most when evaluating fleet management software, how they fit together, and what to look for depending on the size and complexity of your fleet. What is fleet management software? Fleet management software is a platform that tracks, analyses, and helps optimize vehicles, equipment, drivers, and the operational processes around them, typically combining location tracking, fuel monitoring, maintenance scheduling, driver safety, and reporting into one connected system. For fleets running dozens or thousands of assets, that visibility is what turns scattered data into decisions that actually reduce cost and risk. How Does Fleet Management Software Work? Here is how fleet management software typically works, from data capture to action: Data Capture: Sensors on each vehicle or machine continuously collect data on location, fuel, engine status, and driver behaviour. Analysis: The platform analyses that data against defined parameters and assigns a confidence score to flag issues such as fuel waste, harsh braking, or an upcoming maintenance need. Alert: Relevant events surface to the right person in real time, whether that is a safety manager reviewing a violation or a maintenance planner seeing an asset move into an overdue state, with AI Agents able to escalate urgent issues directly to the right person. Report and Act: Dashboards and reports let teams review performance over time, while automated workflows turn insight into action without manual follow-up. Why Is Fleet Management Software Important? Operating a fleet carries a lot of hidden cost. Fuel quietly disappears to idling or theft, a machine breaks down because a preventive service window was missed, and none of this shows up cleanly in a spreadsheet updated once a month. That is why small issues tend to compound instead of getting caught early. Fleet management software solves this by closing the visibility gap in real time, giving operations, maintenance, and finance teams a shared, current view of the same data instead of each working from a different version of it. Key Benefits and Features That Drive Smarter Fleet Operations Here are the features that separate a basic tracking tool from a platform that changes how a fleet is actually run: Real-Time Analytics and Reporting Fleets generate large amounts of data every day: location, fuel consumption, maintenance activity, and driving patterns. Fleet management software turns that raw data into reports and dashboards broken down by driver, vehicle, region, or business unit, so managers can see what is happening without waiting for a scheduled report. AI-Powered Insights and Predictive Analytics AI plays a significant role in fleet management by identifying patterns in the data that a person might miss, such as inefficient driving, a fuel consumption trend moving in the wrong direction, or a maintenance issue likely to surface weeks before it affects operations. Driver Behaviour Monitoring and Safety Scoring Monitoring driver behaviour reduces the chances of accidents because it turns unsafe driving patterns, such as harsh braking and speeding, into a scored, trackable record rather than something a manager learns about only after a complaint or an accident. With performance ranked this way, fleet managers can coach drivers using actual data rather than anecdote. How Does Fleet Management Software Reduce Fuel Costs? Fleet management software reduces fuel costs by distinguishing between fuel used for actual work and fuel lost to idling, and by flagging unexpected drops or refills. That means fuel waste or theft does not go unnoticed until the monthly report arrives, and idling, typically the largest source of wasted fuel, gets caught instead of going undetected. How Does Predictive Maintenance Reduce Downtime? Predictive maintenance reduces downtime by detecting a developing failure before it reaches the point a time-based service schedule would catch it, giving maintenance teams advance notice to act before it turns into a breakdown. Tools that track service intervals against actual usage, whether engine hours or distance covered, and project a machine’s condition against its existing schedule, turn unplanned downtime into a planned maintenance visit. Contract, Cost, and Vendor Management Beyond the vehicles themselves, fleets carry contracts such as leases and insurance policies that are easy to lose track of. Centralizing expiration dates and invoices in the same platform used for operational data helps prevent missed payments and gives finance a clearer picture of true fleet cost. “Fuel consumed during unnecessary idling can represent a measurable operating cost. Independent research on heavy-duty vehicles has recorded diesel consumption of approximately 2.57 litres per hour during idling, while research on diesel vehicles has reported rates as high as 1.85 gallons per hour under certain operating conditions.” Source Types of fleet management software used in various industries Fleet management software is different when used across different industries: In construction and heavy equipment Although telematics-oriented fleet management software is used across various industries, construction companies deploy it in the context of project-based job sites where it is crucial to understand where the vehicle is being underutilized and when a piece of machinery is reaching its maintenance due date. In this case, the emphasis lies on monitoring machine utilization as well as on predictive maintenance. In logistics and transportation In logistics and transportation, fleet management software benefits from monitoring the reliability of routes, fuel costs, and safety of the drivers. Real-time tracking of deliveries and identifying the behaviour of drivers help businesses meet delivery deadlines while saving on almost the only two costs that rise with the fleet size, such as fuel or incidents. In energy, oil, gas and mining industries The fleets operating in this industry do most of their work in dangerous or remote locations; therefore, the importance of compliance reporting, geofencing, or proximity detection rises significantly compared to that in delivery fleets. In Consumer Goods Consumer goods companies run distribution fleets that need to hit tight delivery windows across many stops a day. Route reliability and fuel cost tend to matter most here, alongside visibility into vehicle utilization across large delivery networks. In Maritime and Ports Maritime and port operations manage a mix of vehicles, cranes, and specialized equipment across a single facility. Utilization tracking and maintenance scheduling carry more weight here, since equipment downtime at a port can affect an entire operation’s throughput. In Manufacturing Manufacturing sites run internal fleets of forklifts, loaders, and transport vehicles moving materials between production areas and warehouses. Utilization tracking and preventive maintenance are typically the priority, since unplanned equipment downtime on a production line carries a direct cost. Common challenges The effectiveness of fleet management software depends considerably on the hardware that supplies information to it. If the vehicle does not have an appropriate fuel sensor, for instance, it will not provide any information about the working time compared to idling or about fuel theft; it will only give an approximate total. One should treat sensor coverage not as an issue that can be solved after the implementation has begun, but as a problem that has to be addressed in advance. The implementation of the new platform in a large fleet requires real change management as well. Drivers and technicians who are used to paper records or outdated systems need to be educated and given valid reasons for introducing a new system; otherwise, the software will not be used in the way it was intended. Simply accumulating a lot of information does not guarantee improved choices. If the alerts are not set up with proper boundaries and accountability, employees might find themselves looking at dashboards that no one monitors. The best solution is to set the software up to be useful for a team’s particular needs rather than just flipping it on as if it were preset. Best practices for choosing and implementing fleet management software When evaluating fleet management software, a few factors matter more than the feature list on a sales page: 1. Coverage across your actual asset mix Check whether the platform genuinely supports the equipment types you run, not just standard vehicles, if your fleet includes generators, welding equipment, or heavy machinery alongside trucks. 2. Data you can trust Look for confidence indicators on alerts, such as whether a fuel drop is real or sensor noise, rather than a system that treats every reading as fact. 3. Integration with existing systems The platform should connect with your ERP, finance, or maintenance systems rather than becoming another disconnected data source. 4. Configurability by equipment and location Rules that work for a sedan on a highway should not be forced onto a 30-ton trailer inside a restricted yard. Look for configuration options by machine type and by location. 5. Time to value An implementation of a solution that lasts one year fails to yield ROI because it starts generating savings only when it goes live. It is preferable to ask the vendor to provide a realistic implementation schedule rather than merely demonstrating the features of the solution. TENDERD is an example of the solution that contains all five key aspects: it has an appropriate coverage of various asset classes, the data is made reliable by scoring, it allows for the integration of the system, the configurability of the product is implemented for each machine separately, and its implementation is counted in weeks. As this combination is sometimes difficult to implement late in the project, it should be checked as early as possible. Where TENDERD fits in Fleet data commonly ends up scattered across tools that do not talk to each other: one system for tracking, another for fuel, another for maintenance. TENDERD ‘s platform is built to close that gap for organizations running mixed fleets of vehicles and heavy equipment, not vehicles alone, by putting tracking, fuel, safety, maintenance, and reporting on one shared data record per machine. Three things make TENDERD different in practice. Its fuel intelligence separates working fuel from idling fuel per machine and flags drops or refills with a confidence score, so a fuel investigation starts from evidence rather than a guess. Its proactive maintenance ties preventive schedules, breakdown requests, and parts and labor cost into a single record per machine, tracked through five stages from overdue to completed. And its AI agent capability goes a step further than a dashboard alert: a predictive maintenance agent, for example, can project a developing failure against a machine’s existing service schedule and call the maintenance manager directly when the gap needs closing before the next scheduled visit. Organizations using TENDERD have reported up to a 25% improvement in fuel efficiency, alongside smarter maintenance scheduling and clearer sustainability reporting. Fleets evaluating fleet management software for a mixed vehicle and equipment operation can book a demo to see how t TENDERD’s modules work together on their own data. How TENDERD differs from point solutions Traditional tracking devices have only the main feature of tracking the vehicle, which is why the TENDERD platform stands out from the rest. The table below indicates some direct comparisons between the two methods: Capability Typical single-purpose tracking tool TENDERD Asset coverage Vehicles only Vehicles and heavy/mixed equipment in one platform Real-time visibility GPS location only Live location, geofencing, and CAN bus diagnostics, plus a full per-machine record (documents, specs, violation history) in one profile Driver and operator safety Basic overspeed alert Multiple tracked violation types with driver scoring Utilization and productivity Not tracked, or manual Configurable daily targets by machine type, with drill-down from fleet-level to individual machine performance Fuel investigation Manual reconciliation at month-end Automated drop/refill detection with an event replay Maintenance Separate system, manually scheduled Preventive and reactive maintenance tied to cost, parts, and labor in one record. Response to risk Dashboard alert only AI agents can escalate directly to the right person at the right time. Sustainability reporting Add-on or unavailable Built-in fuel efficiency and emissions reporting. There is certainly a plus of using an integrated platform instead of the regular tracking tool, and it is not just about having more features. It is the fact that there is only one data source not multiple ones. It implies that, thanks to having all fuel, safety, tracking, and maintenance data in one place, a user who would otherwise check three different systems, will simply have one screen to have all the relevant data in one place. “Fragmented fleet data can create measurable administrative and operational inefficiencies. A 2025 U.S. Government Publishing Office audit found that manual and decentralized fleet processes undermined data capture and analysis; in one instance, five vehicles worth approximately $205,700 were not recorded in the organization’s asset system when they entered service.” Source The Bottom Line Fleet management software has progressed well beyond vehicle location tracking. Modern platforms integrate real-time analytics, artificial intelligence-based insights, fuel and upkeep tracking, and security assessments into a cohesive package. Selecting the optimal product requires consideration of your asset combination, extent of user-configurability needed, and urgency in obtaining benefits. For fleets running a mix of vehicles and heavy equipment, TENDERD brings that visibility into a single platform. Book a demo to see how TENDERD’s fleet management software fits your fleet. Frequently Asked Questions What is fleet management software used for? Fleet management software is used to track vehicle and equipment location, monitor fuel consumption and maintenance activity, evaluate driver safety, and generate reports that help fleet managers reduce costs and downtime. Most platforms combine these functions into one connected system rather than requiring separate tools for each task. What does TENDERD do? TENDERD is a fleet and equipment management platform that provides real-time tracking, telematics, utilization monitoring, maintenance insights, and emissions visibility across heavy industries such as construction, logistics, and energy. What fleet and equipment management solutions does TENDERD offer? TENDERD offers GPS tracking, mixed-fleet telematics, utilization analytics, preventive maintenance planning, fuel monitoring, emissions tracking, safety insights, and centralized reporting dashboards. What are the key advantages of using TENDERD for fleet management? TENDERD can help reduce fuel waste, minimize downtime, improve asset utilization, and strengthen compliance reporting by bringing tracking, fuel, maintenance, and safety data into one platform. What does fleet management include? Fleet management typically includes vehicle and equipment tracking, maintenance scheduling, fuel monitoring, driver behavior monitoring, compliance reporting, safety management, performance analytics, and emissions tracking. How can TENDERD help improve fleet productivity and reduce operational costs? TENDERD helps improve productivity and reduce costs by identifying underutilized assets, reducing idle time, automating maintenance alerts, optimizing fuel usage, and centralizing reporting into a single dashboard. What features should I look for in fleet management software? Look for real-time tracking, driver behavior analysis, fuel monitoring with theft and leak detection, and preventive maintenance scheduling, along with reporting that breaks down performance by vehicle, driver, or region. Is fleet management software only for vehicles? No. Many organizations use it to manage a mix of vehicles and heavy equipment, such as generators, welding machines, and construction machinery, especially in construction, energy, and industrial fleets. How long does it take to implement fleet management software? Implementation timelines vary by fleet size and hardware requirements, but a well-scoped rollout typically moves through sensor installation, configuration, and team training in a matter of weeks rather than months.

summary: Successful End-of-Phase 2 meeting with FDA supports advancement of tegoprubart into a global Phase 3 kidney transplantation trial, on track to initiate in late 2026 Long-term Phase 2 BESTOW data presented at ATC 2026 demonstrated sustained higher kidney function and improved patient-reported
body_text: Eledon Pharmaceuticals Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Recent Business Highlights August 13, 2026 PDF Version Successful End-of-Phase 2 meeting with FDA supports advancement of tegoprubart into a global Phase 3 kidney transplantation trial, on track to initiate in late 2026 Long-term Phase 2 BESTOW data presented at ATC 2026 demonstrated sustained higher kidney function and improved patient-reported outcomes with tegoprubart compared with tacrolimus Updated islet cell transplantation data presented at ADA 2026 showed 100% insulin independence in all 12 patients with type 1 diabetes Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments of $88.8 million as of June 30, 2026 IRVINE, Calif., Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Eledon Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (“Eledon”) (Nasdaq: ELDN) today reported its second quarter 2026 operating and financial results and provided recent business highlights. “During the first half of the year, we made meaningful progress establishing the regulatory framework for our planned Phase 3 kidney transplantation program, which we expect to initiate later this year,” said David-Alexandre C. Gros, M.D., Chief Executive Officer of Eledon. “The continued strength of our clinical data, including sustained long-term kidney function in BESTOW and the compelling results from the UChicago Medicine islet cell transplantation study, reinforces the potential of tegoprubart to improve outcomes across multiple transplant settings. We look forward to advancing our Phase 3 program and expanding the clinical evidence for tegoprubart across additional transplant indications.” Second Quarter 2026 Business Highlights Kidney Transplantation Completed a successful End-of-Phase 2 meeting with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, establishing the regulatory framework for the planned Phase 3 trial of tegoprubart in kidney transplantation. The global trial is on track to initiate in late 2026 and enroll approximately 600 patients, with a primary endpoint of non-inferiority versus tacrolimus at 52 weeks based on a composite of biopsy-proven acute rejection (BPAR), graft loss and death. Presented new long-term data from the Phase 2 BESTOW clinical program at the American Transplant Congress (ATC) in June 2026, demonstrating sustained higher kidney function in kidney transplant patients treated with tegoprubart compared with tacrolimus, the current standard-of-care immunosuppression therapy. At 18 months, the eGFR curves showed a statistically significant separation (p<0.05), with mean eGFR approximately 12 mL/min/1.73 m² higher for tegoprubart compared with tacrolimus (approximately 74 vs. 61 mL/min/1.73 m²). No BPAR events were observed in tegoprubart-treated patients after the first six months post-transplant, compared with seven BPAR events (9.4% of tacrolimus-treated patients) reported in the tacrolimus arm. Patient-reported outcomes at 52 weeks favored tegoprubart, with statistically significant improvements versus tacrolimus on two validated measures of symptom burden. Long-term data from the BESTOW extension trial also demonstrated favorable long-term safety and tolerability. Treated the first two patients in an investigator-initiated study of kidney transplant tolerance induction at Massachusetts General Hospital. Entered into a strategic partnership with Natera, Inc., a global leader in cell-free DNA testing and precision medicine, to incorporate Natera’s Prospera kidney transplant assessment test as the exclusive donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) monitoring assay in Eledon’s planned Phase 3 kidney transplantation trial. Islet Cell Transplantation Presented updated data from the University of Chicago Medicine investigator-initiated islet cell transplantation study at ADA 2026. All 12 patients with T1D achieved insulin independence and HbA1c below 6.5%, with a mean most recent HbA1c of approximately 5.4% and no severe hypoglycemic episodes post-transplant. Tegoprubart demonstrated stable islet graft function through a maximum follow-up of 22 months and was generally well tolerated, with no evidence of nephrotoxicity, hypertension or neurotoxicity. Anticipated Upcoming Milestones The Company anticipates the following milestones in 2026 and over the next 12 months: Initiate Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating tegoprubart in kidney transplantation in late 2026. Support the initiation of an investigator-led study evaluating tegoprubart for the prevention of organ rejection in patients with renal dysfunction receiving an islet cell transplant in 2026. Initiate company-sponsored, registration path study evaluating tegoprubart in islet cell transplantation. Support the initiation of an investigator-led study evaluating tegoprubart for the prevention of organ rejection in patients receiving a de novo liver transplant. Receive FDA regulatory guidance on the path to market for tegoprubart in xenotransplantation. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments totaled $88.8 million as of June 30, 2026, compared to $133.3 million as of December 31, 2025. The Company expects current cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments to fund operations into the second quarter of 2027. Research and development (R&D) expenses for the second quarter of 2026 were $18.2 million, including $2.1 million of non-cash stock-based compensation expense, compared to $20.3 million for the comparable period in 2025, including $1.1 million of non-cash stock-based compensation expense. General and administrative (G&A) expenses for the second quarter of 2026 were $4.6 million, including $1.1 million of non-cash stock-based compensation expense, compared to $4.5 million for the comparable period in 2025, including $1.6 million of non-cash stock-based compensation expense. Net loss for the second quarter of 2026 was $31.6 million, or $0.27 per basic common share, compared to a net loss of $11.2 million, or $0.13 per basic common share, for the comparable period in 2025. Net loss in the second quarter of 2026 included a non-cash loss of $9.6 million from changes in the fair value of warrant liabilities, while the 2025 net loss included a non-cash gain of $12.3 million from such changes. Excluding the non-cash items related to changes in the fair value of warrant liabilities, Eledon would have recorded a net loss of $22.0 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, and $23.5 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. About Eledon Pharmaceuticals and tegoprubart Eledon Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is a clinical stage biotechnology company that is developing immune-modulating therapies for the management and treatment of life-threatening conditions. The Company’s lead investigational product is tegoprubart, an anti-CD40L antibody with high affinity for the CD40 Ligand, a well-validated biological target that has broad therapeutic potential. The central role of CD40L signaling in both adaptive and innate immune cell activation and function positions it as an attractive target for non-lymphocyte depleting, immunomodulatory therapeutic intervention. The Company is building upon a deep historical knowledge of anti-CD40L biology to conduct preclinical and clinical studies in kidney allograft transplantation, xenotransplantation, islet cell transplantation, liver transplantation and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Eledon is headquartered in Irvine, California. For more information, please visit the Company’s website at www.eledon.com . title: Palvella Therapeutics Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Corporate Update
summary: First module of the rolling NDA for QTORIN™ rapamycin for microcystic lymphatic malformations submitted to FDA, with completion of the NDA submission on...
body_text: First module of the rolling NDA for QTORIN™ rapamycin for microcystic lymphatic malformations submitted to FDA, with completion of the NDA submission on track for the second half of 2026 Preparing for a planned standalone U.S. commercial launch of QTORIN™ rapamycin for microcystic lymphatic malformations in the first half of 2027, if approved Initiation of Phase 3 trial of QTORIN™ rapamycin for the treatment of cutaneous venous malformations planned for the fourth quarter of 2026 Initiation of Phase 2 trial of QTORIN™ pitavastatin for the treatment of disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis planned for the second half of 2026 Topline results from the Phase 2 LOTU trial of QTORIN™ rapamycin for clinically significant angiokeratomas expected in the second half of 2027 Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments of $250.6 million as of June 30, 2026 Company to host conference call at 8:30 a.m. ET today WAYNE, Pa., Aug. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Palvella Therapeutics, Inc. (Palvella or “the Company”) (Nasdaq: PVLA), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing novel therapies for serious, rare skin diseases and vascular malformations for which there are no U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved therapies, today reported financial results for the second quarter ending June 30, 2026 and provided a corporate update. “We made significant progress during the second quarter, completing our pre-NDA meeting with FDA and initiating the rolling NDA submission for QTORIN™ rapamycin in microcystic lymphatic malformations,” said Wes Kaupinen, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Palvella. “We are working closely with FDA under the program’s Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track designations to expedite development and review, with the objective of potentially introducing the first approved therapy to pediatric and adult patients living with this serious, lifelong disease. Completion of the NDA submission remains on track for the second half of 2026, and we are preparing for a planned standalone commercial launch in the first half of 2027, if approved. We have recruited commercial and medical affairs leaders with deep experience in rare disease and dermatology who are now in the field executing key pre-launch activities, while we continue to advance our other rare disease programs and pursue additional opportunities across the QTORIN™ platform.” Recent Research and Development Highlights QTORIN™ rapamycin for microcystic lymphatic malformations (microcystic LMs) James Treat, M.D., of Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia presented additional Phase 3 SELVA data during a late-breaking session at the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies World Congress (ISSVA), including a statistically significant improvement in the 6–11-year-old cohort and other supportive findings showing improvements in clinical signs and patient-reported outcomes with QTORIN™ rapamycin. Completed an in-person pre-New Drug Application (NDA) meeting with FDA which addressed nonclinical, clinical pharmacology, clinical information, and the planned evidence package for the NDA. Following the pre-NDA meeting, FDA granted Palvella’s request for Rolling Review of the QTORIN™ rapamycin NDA for microcystic LMs, allowing the Agency to begin reviewing completed portions of the application before submission of the full NDA. Submitted the first module of its rolling NDA to the FDA seeking approval of QTORIN™ rapamycin for the treatment of microcystic LMs. The Company remains on track to complete the NDA submission in the second half of 2026. QTORIN™ rapamycin for cutaneous venous malformations (cutaneous VMs) In May 2026, at the 83rd Annual Meeting of the Society for Investigative Dermatology (“SID”), Palvella presented new data from our Phase 2 TOIVA trial of QTORIN™ rapamycin for the treatment of cutaneous VMs highlighting that 100% of patients with bleeding at baseline demonstrated improvement on the Cutaneous Venous Malformations Investigator Global Assessment Bleeding scale at Week 12. Dr. Treat presented additional Phase 2 TOIVA data, including 24-week results, at ISSVA demonstrating statistically significant improvements in both cVM-MCSS Height/Engorgement and cVM-MCSS Appearance at all measured time points, with increasing clinical response observed with longer duration of QTORIN™ rapamycin therapy. Phase 3 trial initiation remains on track for the fourth quarter of 2026 following completion of the planned End-of-Phase 2 meeting. QTORIN™ rapamycin for clinically significant angiokeratomas Dosed the first patients in LOTU, a multicenter Phase 2 trial evaluating Fast Track-designated QTORIN™ rapamycin for clinically significant angiokeratomas, a rare, chronic and debilitating isolated lymphatic malformation affecting an estimated more than 50,000 diagnosed patients in the U.S. and for which there are no FDA-approved therapies. Topline results from LOTU are expected in the second half of 2027. QTORIN™ pitavastatin for disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis (DSAP) Palvella's second product candidate, QTORIN™ pitavastatin, is for the treatment of disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis, a premalignant genetic skin disease that presents as persistent, often extensive lesions that enlarge and increase in size, number, and extent over time, causing chronic loss of skin integrity which can severely impact quality-of-life; no FDA-approved therapies currently exist for the estimated more than 50,000 diagnosed patients in the U.S. Strengthened the intellectual property position supporting QTORIN™ pitavastatin through the issuance of U.S. Patent No. 12,636,273, exclusively licensed from Yale University and building on pioneering work by Keith Choate, M.D., Ph.D. The issued claims cover the topical administration of HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, including pitavastatin, for the treatment of porokeratosis, including DSAP, and provide protection into 2043. Phase 2 trial initiation expected in the second half of 2026. QTORIN™ rapamycin and QTORIN™ platform expansion Palvella plans to announce the fourth target clinical indication for QTORIN™ rapamycin in the second half of 2026. The expansion of QTORIN™ rapamycin into additional indications is supported by a growing body of published literature highlighting the broad potential of rapamycin in several difficult-to-treat, mTOR-driven skin diseases while advocating for targeted, topical approaches suited to improve tolerability and safety. Palvella plans to announce the third product candidate from the QTORIN™ platform in a serious, rare disease with no FDA-approved therapies in the second half of 2026. Recent Corporate Highlights Appointed accomplished rare disease biotech executive and commercial leader Matt Pauls, J.D., M.B.A., to the Board of Directors, further strengthening the Board with extensive experience in rare disease drug development, commercialization, and corporate strategy from executive and Board roles at Savara Inc., Soleno Therapeutics, Strongbridge Biopharma, and Insmed Incorporated. Awarded “Healthcare & Life Sciences Company of the Year” at the 2026 Philadelphia Alliance for Capital and Technology Ecosystem Awards, recognizing Palvella's leadership in advancing innovative therapies for rare diseases and its contributions to the region's life sciences ecosystem. Completed the uplisting to the Nasdaq Global Market, providing increased visibility within the investment community and reflecting the Company’s continued growth and achievement of key corporate milestones. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments as of June 30, 2026 were $250.6 million. Research and development expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $12.5 million, as compared to $5.1 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. title: Serve Teams Up with Wonder and Grubhub Amid a New Wave of Expansion
summary: New cities, new delivery platform partners, and even the first talking delivery robot. Those are just a few of the announcements we’re making today as we continue to expand our capabilities and put our technology to work for more consumers, businesses, and teams than ever before.
body_text: Back Serve Teams Up with Wonder and Grubhub Amid a New Wave of Expansion S e r v e T e a m s U p w i t h W o n d e r a n d G r u b h u b A m i d a N e w W a v e o f E x p a n s i o n Article August 17, 2026 Serve Teams Up with Wonder and Grubhub Amid a New Wave of Expansion Serve Teams Up with Wonder and Grubhub Amid a New Wave of Expansion Article Not long ago, our robots were delivering dinner in a handful of neighborhoods. Today, they’re entering new markets from San Jose to the nation’s capital, joining more delivery platforms, and helping us build a broader physical AI platform that extends from sidewalks into hospitals. Today we announced a new partnership with Grubhub, a subsidiary of Wonder, bringing Serve robot delivery to the Grubhub marketplace beginning in Chicago, Los Angeles, and Alexandria. The launch marks our first collaboration with Wonder and Grubhub and makes Grubhub the latest major delivery platform on Serve’s network. And that’s just one part of what we’re announcing. We’ve also launched in Washington, DC and San Jose. We’re preparing to open our first micro depots in Miami. Diligent Robotics has begun rolling out the next generation of Moxi to hospitals. We’re previewing a new restaurant product called Beacon, and Serve Advertising is launching Characters, a new kind of interactive brand experience built on our robots. Each announcement is different, but together they point in the same direction. We’re building more ways for robots to do useful work alongside humans in the real world. Wonder and Grubhub Join Serve’s Delivery Network Our new partnership brings Serve robot delivery to Grubhub customers in Chicago, Los Angeles, and Alexandria. At Wonder’s Alexandria location, customers ordering through Grubhub will also be able to receive eligible orders through Serve’s autonomous delivery network. For Serve, adding another major delivery platform means more opportunities for our robots to make deliveries. More order volume can help put the fleet to work more often while giving restaurants another way to reach customers. That is an important part of how we think about scale. Expanding autonomous delivery isn’t only about putting more robots on sidewalks. It’s also about making better use of the fleet and operations already in place. Hello, San Jose and Washington, DC We’re also welcoming two new major markets to Serve’s growing map. Serve has launched in Washington, DC and San Jose, California , seventh and eighth major U.S. markets, both in partnership with DoorDash. Together, the two metros reach a population of 8 million and expand Serve’s geographic coverage as we continue growing delivery volume. The launches join Los Angeles, Chicago, Atlanta, Dallas, and Miami on Serve’s growing map as we continue expanding our national delivery network. Every city is different. New streets, neighborhoods, merchants, customers, weather, and pedestrian environments all create new operating experience for the fleet. That real-world experience is central to how we build robots that can work in human environments. A Smaller Footprint for Entering New Neighborhoods We’re also changing the infrastructure behind the fleet. In Miami, we’re preparing to open Serve’s first micro depot , a new class of small-footprint operating site that handles robot staging, charging, dispatch, and maintenance without the build-out time of a full-scale facility. Micro depots require minimal infrastructure and can be set up rapidly in high-demand neighborhoods, giving us a repeatable way to enter new neighborhoods and cities faster and at lower cost. Moxi 2.0 Starts Rolling Into Hospitals Our work is expanding indoors, too. Diligent Robotics, a Serve Robotics company, has begun rolling out the next generation of Moxi to health systems including Endeavor Health Edward Hospital in the Chicago area, Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Los Angeles, and Children’s Hospital Los Angeles. Moxi 2.0 can perceive and interpret its surroundings up to 15 times faster than before, has 10 times the onboard compute, and includes improved autonomy and decision making along with upgraded sensors and storage. It can also operate for up to 18 hours with 30% faster battery charging, all without requiring changes to existing hospital infrastructure. Those upgrades help Moxi react more quickly to dynamic hospital environments, including crowded hallways, opening elevator doors, and shifting foot traffic. Moxi 2.0 builds on deliveries completed across 25+ U.S. hospitals and introduces Diligent’s World Model, a learning system that improves every robot with the experience of the whole fleet. Meet Beacon, a Simpler Connection Between Restaurants and Robots We’re also previewing Beacon , a standalone countertop product that will connect restaurants, customers, and Serve robots. With built-in cellular connectivity, Beacon will alert restaurant staff the moment a robot arrives for pickup and will require nothing from a restaurant beyond power. There’s no tablet, no additional hardware, and no changes to existing systems. Beacon is designed to speed up pickup for current restaurant partners while extending robot delivery to restaurants whose back-of-house setups previously could not support it. Serve Advertising Launches Characters, With Chomp Finally, our robots are getting a little more personality. Serve Advertising is launching Characters , a new product that expands what brands can do with Serve’s robots. Advertisers have long been able to wrap Serve robots in custom designs. Characters adds a personality. Brands can now create a character that customers can talk with in real time, powered by a curated conversational AI model and developed together by Serve and the advertiser. The first Character is Chomp , co-created with Grubhub. He’s a talking, hamburger-wrapped robot who treats every delivery like a very important mission. Chomp will appear across social media and select customer experiences featuring Grubhub gift cards and swag. Following the launch, other brands will have the opportunity to explore similar activations through Serve Advertising. More Demand. More Places. More Robot Sidekicks. Taken separately, today’s announcements span delivery platforms, cities, operations, hospitals, restaurant hardware, and advertising. Together, they reflect the same approach we’ve had from the beginning. We build technology that can do useful work alongside people, then keep finding ways to make that technology more capable and more widely available. We’re excited to welcome Wonder and Grubhub to the network, and even more excited about what we can build from here.

body_text: View All News SES AI’s UZ Energy Becomes Sol-Ark® Certified Battery Partner August 12, 2026 Positions UZ Energy to Compete for Battery Sales Within Sol-Ark ® Eco-System Three UZ Energy Low-Voltage Residential Batteries Certified for Closed-Loop Compatibility US Energy Distributors Named Master Distributor and Primary U.S. Contact for UZ Energy WOBURN, Mass.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- SES AI Corporation (“SES AI”) (NYSE: SES), a global leader in the development and manufacturing of AI-enhanced high-performance Li-Metal and Li-ion batteries, today announced that UZ Energy, an SES AI company, has become a Sol-Ark® certified battery partner and has named US Energy Distributors as the master distributor for UZ Energy’s battery products in the United States. With this certification, UZ Energy is positioned to compete for battery sales within an established market from the outset and to capture market share as Sol-Ark installers, distributors, and customers evaluate new certified energy-storage configurations. “Expanding UZ Energy’s presence in the United States is an important part of SES AI’s energy storage strategy,” said Dr. Qichao Hu, SES AI founder and CEO. “Certification with Sol-Ark connects UZ Energy to a large and established residential energy storage ecosystem and creates an immediate path to compete for U.S. battery sales. This certification also provides installers and distribution partners access to a broader range of integrated storage configurations while supporting the continued commercial growth of the UZ Energy platform.” UZ Energy will be listed under Sol-Ark® low voltage (48V) certified battery partners. UZ Energy’s three low-voltage residential batteries are certified for closed-loop compatibility with the Sol-Ark 12K-2P-LL, 15K-2P and 18K-2P Hybrid Inverters. The certification combines Sol-Ark’s hybrid inverter technology and established installer ecosystem with UZ Energy’s lithium iron phosphate battery systems, creating additional residential energy-storage configurations for installers, distributors and homeowners across the United States. Sol-Ark has established a substantial U.S. residential energy-storage ecosystem spanning its hybrid inverters, certified battery partners, distributors and installer network. The certified UZ Energy residential battery portfolio includes: UZ Energy L051100-B 5.12kWh Power Lite Series; UZ Energy PLPA-L1-10K2-U Power Lite Plus Series; and UZ Energy IG-16K-U 16kWh Power Lite Plus Series. The certification follows technical integration testing of the UZ Energy battery platform, including closed-loop communication, operating performance and protection functionality. About SES AI SES AI Corp. (NYSE: SES) is powering the future of global electric transportation on land and in the air with the world’s most advanced Li-Metal batteries. SES AI is the first battery company in the world to accelerate its pace of innovation by utilizing superintelligent AI across the spectrum of its business, from research and development; materials sourcing; cell design; engineering and manufacturing; to battery health and safety monitoring. Founded in 2012, SES AI is an Li-Metal battery developer and manufacturer headquartered in Boston and with operations in Singapore, Shanghai, and Seoul. Learn more at SES.AI . About UZ Energy UZ Energy provides residential, commercial and industrial energy storage systems. The company designs and manufactures lithium iron phosphate battery solutions engineered for safety, reliability, scalability and long operating life. UZ Energy’s portfolio includes low-voltage residential batteries, high-voltage commercial storage systems and integrated energy-storage solutions serving international markets. UZ Energy is an SES AI company. About Sol-Ark® Sol-Ark provides intelligent solar and energy-storage solutions for residential, commercial and industrial applications. Its hybrid inverter platforms support grid-connected, whole-home backup and off-grid applications through flexible system architecture and compatibility with an extensive ecosystem of certified battery manufacturers. Founded by veterans and defense engineers, we design and manufacture our own hybrid inverter and energy storage technology, bringing industry-leading efficiency, flexibility, and power into a single, all-in-one solution. About US Energy Distributors US Energy Distributors, Inc. is a U.S.-based distributor of residential and commercial solar, battery-storage and power-conversion equipment. The company works with manufacturers, installers, project developers and regional distributors to bring advanced energy products to the U.S. market. US Energy Distributors serves as the master distributor and primary U.S. sales and sub-distribution contact for UZ Energy battery products. title: What Community Means at Alaan
body_text: Eight months ago, we asked ourselves a simple question: Where do finance professionals go to connect beyond boardrooms? Finance isn’t just about numbers—it’s about the people behind them. But there wasn’t a space where finance professionals could openly share ideas, learn from each other, and build real connections. So, we decided to build it. One simple question guided everything we did. From the very beginning everything we did was shaped by one core principle: Does this add value? If it didn’t help finance professionals grow, connect, or learn—we didn’t do it. That principle became the foundation of everything that followed. It started with a simple idea: good chai and great conversations. The first step was ChAI with Alaan—a gathering of thirty finance professionals, talking about chai, AI, and everything in between. We weren’t sure what to expect, but what happened in that room was special. People weren’t just attending—they were staying back, exchanging ideas, and having conversations that went beyond their day-to-day work. That’s when we knew this was more than just an event. And that was just the beginning. A space for finance professionals to learn, connect, and grow. As the community grew, so did the conversations. In our Chief Future Officer series CFOs started sharing their journeys, giving insight into leadership, decision-making, and the challenges they had faced. More events followed—some small and interactive, others larger with fireside chats on the future of finance. We wanted to bring finance professionals together, not just in person but wherever they were, so we launched online webinars to make these discussions accessible to everyone. We also realized that finance professionals needed more than just conversations—they needed resources. That’s where Alaan Academy came in. A growing library of insights, guides, and tools designed to help finance professionals stay ahead. A community that extends beyond events. As more people joined the conversation, it became clear that these discussions needed a home beyond our events and webinars. That’s when we started what is now the FinTalk community —an online space where finance professionals could ask questions, exchange knowledge, and support each other in real time. Then came Job Vault , an initiative to help finance professionals find and access relevant career opportunities. Because a strong community isn’t just about conversations—it’s about helping each other grow. And we’ve been adding to it ever since. From an Idea to a loved community. What started as an experiment has grown into something bigger than we ever imagined. But the purpose remains the same: to add value. To those who have been part of this journey—thank you. To those considering joining—we’d love to have you. This isn’t just a network. It’s a community built on real conversations, shared experiences, and meaningful connections. And we’re just getting started. ‍

title: Frozen Yogurt vs Ice Cream: What’s the Difference?
summary: Frozen yogurt vs ice cream: how they're made, how they differ in fat, sugar, and calories, plus which one is the better pick.
body_text: Published on May 8th, 2025 Updated on August 7th, 2026 In this article What is frozen yogurt? What is ice cream? History of frozen yogurt Is frozen yogurt healthier than ice cream? Which is better for diabetics, ice cream or frozen yogurt? YOLO, SO FRO-YO YOUR WAY TO HAPPINESS FOR DESSERT Azucar Ice Cream In the battle of delicious frozen desserts, frozen yogurt often takes a back seat to gelato , frozen custard , and ice cream . And that’s too bad, because frozen yogurt is delicious! It’s the perfect treat for hot summer nights when you want something a bit lighter and a bit more refreshing. (Plus, the self-serve places have all those fun mix-ins, and you can’t beat that.) But do you know exactly what fro-yo is? When it comes to frozen yogurt vs ice cream, here’s what the differences actually are. What is frozen yogurt? Although the name might make you think it’s possible, you actually can’t just throw a pint of yogurt into the freezer and call it frozen yogurt. Frozen yogurt the dessert is actually made from a mixture of yogurt, milk, and sugar. First, manufacturers mix the milk and sugar together and pasteurize it, then they add the yogurt. Once it’s all blended, it rests for several hours and then goes into the freezer to become the dessert we know and love. If the frozen yogurt isn’t flavored with anything (like chocolate, strawberry, mint, cookie dough, or anything else you can find to use), the flavor will be tangy and sweet, with a delightfully creamy texture. What is ice cream? Ice cream is similar to frozen yogurt, except it’s made with cream instead of yogurt. Manufacturers blend together milk, sugar, cream, and sometimes egg yolks before freezing it. The United States actually has a requirement that all ice cream must have at least 10% milkfat, so expect a creamier texture and more fat content than frozen yogurt. Sloan’s Ice Cream Leopold’s Ice Cream History of frozen yogurt Yogurt itself may be an ancient food, but frozen yogurt is much younger — it was invented in the 1970s, under the unfortunate name of “frogurt.” The creator was a company called HP Hood, now known as Dairy Foods. Bloomingdale’s had asked HP Hood for a low-fat frozen treat they could bring into stores, and frozen yogurt was born. By the end of the 1970s, fro-yo was being sold across the country. The first frozen yogurt chain opened in New York, then another opened in Massachusetts, and we haven’t turned back since. Is frozen yogurt healthier than ice cream? Honestly, it depends! On the surface, it seems so — frozen yogurt has less calories and less fat than ice cream. But it probably also has more sugar. And if you pile on toppings like you would at a self-serve fro-yo spot, you’re probably scaring any health benefits away. From a probiotic standpoint, frozen yogurt is better for your gut health. Regardless, though, either ice cream or frozen yogurt can be enjoyed in moderation and be a perfectly fine and healthy snack. So what is a healthy ice cream alternative? Gelato has a lot less fat, but that needs as much moderation as ice cream and frozen yogurt. Sorbet and Italian ice could be good options, too, but watch for the sugar content. Your best bet is to make faux ice cream using bananas, where you freeze banana slices and then use a food processor to transform them into a creamy dessert similar to ice cream. You can add mix-ins like dark chocolate and peanut butter, or make it a little creamier by adding plant-based milk. Either way, it’s a delicious low-calorie dessert that scratches that ice cream itch. Which is better for diabetics, ice cream or frozen yogurt? It may come as a surprise, but the best dessert for diabetics between ice cream and frozen yogurt is good old ice cream. Frozen yogurt sounds like — and often is touted as — a healthier alternative, but producers need to jam it full of sugar to offset the tartness of the yogurt itself. Ice cream generally has less sugar and less carbs. That being said, ice cream should certainly be eaten in moderation. It still has sugar in it, too! And if you add toppings like hot fudge and whipped cream, you could be creating a diabetic disaster zone. If ice cream is the winner in your mind for the epic ice cream vs frozen yogurt battle, you’re in luck. Goldbelly can deliver your favorite ice cream pint straight to your door. title: Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) is now available in the Canada West (Calgary) Region (ca-west-1)
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) is now available in the Canada West (Calgary) Region (ca-west-1)
body_text: Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) is now available in the Canada West (Calgary) Region (ca-west-1), allowing customers in the Canada West Region to build Cassandra-compatible applications with lower latency while keeping their data within the Region to meet data residency requirements. Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) is a scalable, highly available, and managed Apache Cassandra–compatible database service. Amazon Keyspaces is serverless, so you pay for only the resources that you use and you can build applications that serve thousands of requests per second with virtually unlimited throughput and storage. This regional expansion enables organizations in Canada to build highly scalable, low-latency applications using familiar Cassandra Query Language (CQL) without the operational burden of managing Cassandra clusters. To learn more about on Keyspaces, visit the Amazon Keyspaces documentation .

John Turner, President & CEO, commented, "Power is where our growth is going, and we are building it contract-first. Our oilfield power division continues to scale and we expect 180 to 200 MWs deployed by the end of this year. In the second quarter we signed our first long-term behind-the-meter contract, for 120 MWs expected to come online at the end of the first quarter of 2027, and we put mobile power on that site immediately to keep the customer running through construction. That is the whole point. Data center customers want one partner to solve the entire power problem, not a generator supplier, and solving it starts on day one rather than the day the permanent plant is finished. Since signing the Global Framework Agreement with Caterpillar, the opportunities in front of us have grown in scale, duration and scope. We are in active negotiations now, and we will announce equipment placements and economics when contracts are signed, not before." “Atlas’ status as the leading provider of sand and logistics in the West Texas market has positioned us to be selective about the work going forward we secure as the proppant market begins to recover. With the productive capacity of some of our competitors’ mines potentially impaired by lack of sustaining investment, we believe the sand market is currently close to balance and positioned for further tightening in 2027. Atlas is positioning itself to maximize its advantages both for itself and its key customers in a market where we believe supplier execution will be at a premium.” Bud Brigham, Executive Chairman, said, “Our excitement and optimism in private power lie in the fact that we have the right equipment, the right strategy and, most importantly, the right people. I could not be more excited about the opportunities we are currently working on and sharing more information about those projects in the not-so-distant future when able.” Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Second quarter 2026 total revenue increased $27.7 million, or 10.4% when compared to the first quarter of 2026, to $293.2 million. Product revenue decreased by $5.4 million, or 5.0% when compared to the first quarter of 2026, to $103.5 million. Second quarter 2026 proppant product sales volumes were 5.6 million tons. Service revenue increased $23.6 million, or 17.0% when compared to the first quarter of 2026, to $162.7 million. Second quarter 2026 rental revenue increased $9.5 million, or 54.3% when compared to the first quarter of 2026, to $27.0 million. Second quarter 2026 cost of sales (excluding depreciation, depletion and accretion expense) (“cost of sales”) increased by $7.3 million, or 3.4% when compared to the first quarter of 2026, to $221.3 million. Cost of sales consisted of $66.1 million of proppant plant and logistics equipment operating costs, $1.4 million from power equipment costs, $140.7 million related to service costs, $8.8 million related to rental costs and $4.3 million in royalties. Selling, general and administrative expenses for the second quarter of 2026 increased by $3.7 million when compared to the first quarter of 2026, to $39.4 million or 10.4%. Net loss for the second quarter of 2026 was $25.1 million, and Adjusted EBITDA for the second quarter of 2026 was $49.5 million. Liquidity, Capital Expenditures and Other As of June 30, 2026, the Company’s total liquidity was $292.9 million, which was comprised of $168.2 million in cash and cash equivalents, and $124.7 million of availability under the Company’s 2023 ABL Credit Facility. Individuals wishing to participate in the conference call should dial (877) 407-4133. A live webcast will be available at https://ir.atlas.energy/ . Please access the webcast or dial in for the call at least 10 minutes ahead of the start time to ensure a proper connection. An archived version of the conference call will be available on the Company’s website shortly after the conclusion of the call. About Atlas Energy Solutions Atlas Energy Solutions Inc. (NYSE: AESI) is a leading energy solutions provider, unlocking energy that powers the world’s critical infrastructure. For companies requiring power where grid utilities are unavailable, Atlas can help customers overcome the schedule and capital expense barriers that hinder project and operational success. For oil & gas producers, Atlas helps companies overcome disruptive operational and technical challenges to maximize oilfield completions and operations. From large scale private grid power systems to the world’s most advanced frac sand delivery networks, Atlas delivers the engineering, technology and turnkey project execution expertise that turns energy constraints into advantages. are non-GAAP supplemental financial measures used by our management and by external users of our financial statements such as investors, research analysts and others, in the case of Adjusted EBITDA, to assess our consolidated operating performance on a consistent basis across periods by removing the effects of development activities, provide views on capital resources available to organically fund growth projects and, in the case of Adjusted Free Cash Flow, assess the financial performance of our assets and their ability to sustain dividends or reinvest to organically fund growth projects over the long term without regard to financing methods, capital structure, or historical cost basis. These measures do not represent and should not be considered alternatives to, or more meaningful than, net income, income from operations, net cash provided by operating activities or any other measure of financial performance presented in accordance with GAAP as measures of our financial performance. Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted Free Cash Flow have important limitations as analytical tools because they exclude some but not all items that affect net income, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure. Our computation of Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA Margin, Adjusted Free Cash Flow, Adjusted Free Cash Flow Margin, Adjusted Free Cash Flow Conversion, Maintenance Capital Expenditures and Adjusted Cash SG&A may differ from computations of similarly titled measures of other companies. Non-GAAP Measure Definitions: We define Adjusted EBITDA as net income before depreciation, depletion and accretion, amortization expense of acquired intangible assets, interest expense, income tax expense, stock and unit-based compensation, loss on extinguishment of debt, loss on disposal of assets, insurance recovery (gain), litigation-related costs, net, unrealized commodity derivative gain (loss), other acquisition related costs, and other non-recurring costs. Management believes Adjusted EBITDA is useful because it allows management to more effectively evaluate the Company’s consolidated operating performance and compare the results of its operations from period to period and against our peers without regard to financing method or capital structure. We exclude the items listed above from net income in arriving at Adjusted EBITDA because these amounts can vary substantially from company to company within our industry depending upon accounting methods and book values of assets, capital structures and the method by which the assets were acquired. Certain prior period litigation-related costs, net are now included as an add-back to Adjusted EBITDA in order to conform to the current period presentation and to more accurately describe the Company’s consolidated operating performance and results period over period. We define Adjusted EBITDA Margin as Adjusted EBITDA divided by total revenue. We define Adjusted Free Cash Flow as Adjusted EBITDA less Maintenance Capital Expenditures. Management believes that Adjusted Free Cash Flow is useful to investors as it provides a measure of the ability of our business to generate cash. We define Adjusted Free Cash Flow Margin as Adjusted Free Cash Flow divided by total revenue. We define Adjusted Free Cash Flow Conversion as Adjusted Free Cash Flow divided by Adjusted EBITDA. We define Maintenance Capital Expenditures as capital expenditures excluding growth capital expenditures, reconstruction of previously incurred growth capital expenditures, equipment assets acquired through debt, and asset retirement obligations. We define Adjusted Cash SG&A as selling, general and administrative expenses (“SG&A”) less stock-based compensation, depreciation in SG&A, non-recurring transaction expenses, and certain litigation expenses and insurance proceeds in SG&A.
